Similarity grades the subject art (bounding-box cropped) with classical metrics (dhash, phash, global SSIM, color histogram) - no learned embedding.
A model sheet is a collage of panels: the best-matching reference region is reported alongside the full-frame score, and the similarity grade uses the best region.

Identity limit, measured in calibration: against a multi-panel model sheet these metrics cannot confirm WHICH character is drawn (a wrong character graded about the same as the right one). For identity-grade gating, pass the approved same-class comp (the locked design or start still) as the reference; against a sheet, the discriminating evidence is the proportion report, the color_histogram part, and the text check.

Proportion compares bounding-box share of frame; it assumes candidate and reference are the same framing class (sticker vs sticker, scene vs scene). Against a model sheet, whose foreground saturates the frame, it reads as 'how much smaller is the candidate's art than the sheet's coverage' - which is exactly the oversized/undersized emblem signal it was built to catch.
OCR is unavailable on this deployment, so lettering inside the art is not machine-read here; run the native-resolution zoom audit before shipping anything the OCR component could not read.

Video drift_score is the worst sampled frame's similarity drift (no proportion term: frames and the reference still are the same framing class by construction).
Each sampled frame is graded against the reference with the same subject-crop metrics as /check-image; the verdict rides on the worst frame.
Frozen detection compares difference hashes of consecutive sampled frames (similarity >= 0.97); fine motion smaller than the sampling interval can be missed - sample more frames for short clips.
